sources.title: Masters (2021): Traditional food plants of the upper Aswa River catchment of northern Uganda - a cultural crossroads
reviewLocators: Oxalis corniculata table row: leaf; SA45 field identifier
sources.geographicContext: Upper Aswa River catchment, northern Uganda
sources.limitation: Ethnographic food-processing report, not a cooking-safety trial, Philippine practice, oxalate-removal validation, safe serving or clinical regimen. Neighboring greens' sauces and repeated-boiling instructions are not transferred.
sources.reuseReview: Educational summary only. The study records a no-commercial-use assurance to participants; public reuse/context review remains pending despite the open-access article license.

sources.title: Gul et al. (2011): Evaluation of Abelmoschus moschatus extracts for antioxidant, free radical scavenging, antimicrobial and antiproliferative activities using in vitro assays
sources.materialProvenance: Seeds and leaves supplied by CIMAP Regional Centre Hyderabad, India; no specimen voucher accession recorded in reviewed plant-material paragraph.
sources.experimentalModel: In vitro assays; not a human trial
sources.limitation: Water extraction, centrifugation and vacuum concentration are laboratory descriptions, not a household decoction, coffee-flavouring recipe, food-grade seed process, cancer treatment or human dose.

proposals.preparationPart: Leaves; not other Oxalis species or neighboring vegetables
proposals.preparationDescription: Masters' northern Uganda ethnobotanical study lists Oxalis corniculata leaves among vegetables traditionally parboiled before further preparation. This is a source-reported food-processing description, not a complete beginner recipe or treatment. The study does not establish a safe serving, validated oxalate removal or species-specific cooking time; PROSEA's oxalate warning remains applicable to this held draft.

proposals.preparationPart: Seeds and leaves processed separately; not essential oil or okra
proposals.preparationDescription: Gul and colleagues cleaned, shade-dried and coarsely powdered Abelmoschus moschatus seeds and leaves separately. Their in vitro study prepared water extracts from the powders, centrifuged the suspensions and concentrated the collected liquid with a vacuum evaporator. This laboratory description is not a home recipe or treatment, does not establish safe ingestion or a human dose, and supplies no coffee-flavouring process.

identityReview.finding: The flora retains Blanco's misapplied Ocimum virgatum under O. tenuiflorum. This does not reconcile the book's O. gratissimum association.

occurrenceReview.finding: No Philippines mention was found in this bounded PDF text search; omission is not absence. No current Philippine range or common-name reassignment is adopted.

excludedFromAdoption: Borrowing neighboring vegetable recipes, sauce ingredients or boiling repetitions
Claiming that parboiling eliminates oxalate toxicity or creates a safe amount
Treating in vitro antioxidant or antiproliferative assays as human treatment evidence
Experimental extraction ratios, heat levels, durations or stock concentrations as household directions
Kastuli seed essential oil, perfume, incense, tobacco or other Abelmoschus species' recipes
Inferring Lokoloko's absence from country-list omission or relabelling it as holy basil
remainingGaps: Lokoloko remains partial and identity/occurrence held.
Kastuli seed food-grade and coffee processing remain unestablished.
Oxalis safe serving, oxalate controls and beginner recipe remain unvalidated.
Eleven covers, human/category/botanical review, source-reuse review, backup, transactional duplicates and isolated database tests remain pending.
